text.p: Following are some major events to have occurred on May 28 in history:
1156 - William of Sicily crushed a revolt against his rule, defeating the Byzantine fleet at Brindisi.

1738 - Joseph Ignace Guillotin, French physician and advocate of humane capital punishment, born. The first execution using the decapitation machine that would later bear his name took place on April 25, 1792.

1759 - William Pitt the Younger, English statesman and politician, born. He became Britain's youngest prime minister in 1783, holding office until 1801 and returning to the post in 1804 during the Napoleonic wars.
1849 - Anne Bronte, English novelist and sister of Charlotte and Emily Bronte, died. Under the pseudonym of Acton Bell, she wrote "The Tenant of Wildfell Hall".

1884 - Eduard Benes, Czechoslovakian statesman, born. A founder of modern Czechoslovakia, he was foreign minister from 1918 to 1935 and president from 1935 to 1938. Fleeing his homeland to escape the Nazi invaders he returned after World War Two and served as president again until the communist takeover in 1948.
1925 - Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau, German baritone, born. Known for his performance of opera, notably Mozart, Strauss and Wagner, he is also famed for his interpretation of German lieder.
1937 - In Britain, Neville Chamberlain took over as prime minister at the head of a coalition government following Stanley Baldwin's retirement.
1940 - Belgium's King Leopold surrendered to Nazi Germany.
1940 - Norwegian and British forces captured Narvik in Norway.
1940 - Evacuation of the defeated Allied armies from Dunkirk began. By its completion on the night of June 2, a total of 224,585 British and 112,546 French and Belgian troops had been saved.
1972 - The Duke of Windsor, Britain's former King Edward VIII who abdicated in 1936 amidst a constitutional crisis, died in Paris.
1981 - Cardinal Stefan Wyszynski, Poland's Catholic Primate and staunch oppoent of Warsaw's communist authorities, died.
1982 - Pope John Paul II arrived in Britain on the first Papal visit there since 1531.
1982 - In the Falklands war, British troops recaptured Port Darwin and Goose Green from the Argentine army, taking at least 1,400 prisoners.
1987 - A 19-year-old West German, Mathias Rust, flew his light plane from Helsinki to Moscow, passing through Soviet airspace unchallenged and eventually landing on Red Square.
1991 - NATO defence ministers approved a radical shakeup of its forces in post-cold war Europe, including creation of a Rapid Reaction Force.
1991 - In Ethiopia, rebel tanks blasted their way into Addis Ababa at dawn, toppling the remnants of a Marxist government whose 17-year rule brought war and famine.
1995 - Russia's worst recorded earthquake killed 1,989 people in the Far East oil-producing town of Neftegorsk, on the north of Sakhalin Island. The quake measured 7.5 on the Richter scale.
1995 - Bosnia's Foreign Minister Irfan Ljubijankic was killed when his helicopter was downed in a rocket attack near the Croatian border.
1996 - President Jacques Chirac announced France would end military conscription from 1997, earlier than previously planned.
